title: Extension of semiabelian homomorphisms over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its fraction field, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G,H\to T$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Here a commutative group scheme over $T$ consists of multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over $T$ satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Set $G_F=G\times_T\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $H_F=H\times_T\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-pc-base-change]. Every $F$-group homomorphism $v:G_F\to H_F$ extends to a unique $T$-group homomorphism $\widetilde v:G\to H$. No completeness, excellence or residue-field perfection hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: G. Faltings, Finiteness Theorems for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields, Arithmetic Geometry (1986), Chapter II, section 2, Lemma 1, printed pp.10-11: the complete-DVR extension input in the opening sentence, and descent from completion for the DVR formulation. Local copy WANTED; primary-source scan read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~lefourns/contenu/Zywina/Faltings.pdf . The arbitrary-DVR formulation is an agent-extracted local input, not a verbatim theorem of the scan.

proof.text: The generic fibre $P=H_F$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of $H$, hence is closed (on affine charts base change of a quotient algebra is the same quotient after tensoring). A finite affine presentation of $H$ gives a finite cover of $P$ by the algebras $C[1/\pi]$, each finitely presented over $F$, for a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Thus $P$ is separated of finite type. Its semiabelian geometric-fibre condition is the restriction of [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres] to geometric points over $F$. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-neron-lft-existence] to obtain $(N,\alpha)$. Its group-homomorphism mapping property, with the smooth groups $H$ and $G$, gives $j:H\to N$ and $f:G\to N$ satisfying $\alpha j_F=1_P$ and $\alpha f_F=v$.

source.place: Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models (1990), 10.1 Definition 1 (printed p.289) and 10.2 Theorem 2 (printed p.297), specialized to geometrically semiabelian groups. Local copy WANTED; primary-source scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf, PDF pages 296 and 304. The criterion uses absence of an additive subgroup after completed strict henselian fraction-field extension, which holds for a geometrically semiabelian group.

proof.text: The map $j$ is already a $T$-group homomorphism and $j_F=\alpha^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-generically-isomorphic-semiabelian-open-immersion] with $A=H$, $B=N$, $a=j$: $H$ has all the required finite-presentation and semiabelian-fibre hypotheses, and $N$ is smooth and separated; the criterion requires no finite-type hypothesis on $N$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], identify $H$ with the open subgroup scheme $U=j(H)\subseteq N$.

source.place: Agent generalization of Brian Conrad, Semistable reduction for abelian varieties, proof of Theorem 4.4, printed pp.12–16, especially Corollary 3.3, Lemma 4.9 and the quasi-finite birational argument. Local copy WANTED; primary lecture notes read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/DarmonCM/2011Notes/SemistableReduction.pdf . The theorem as printed has abelian generic fibre and Néron target; this statement extracts the proof for a GIVEN generically isomorphic homomorphism, where only smoothness and separatedness of the target are used. It is an agent-extracted lemma, not a verbatim assertion of Theorem 4.4.

proof.text: Fix a geometric closed fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Its group $G_\Omega$ satisfies the exact-sequence hypothesis of [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] by [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]; smoothness follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and finite type and separatedness follow by the charts of step 1. The integrality statement at $n=1$ makes $G_\Omega$ connected. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], the identity component $C=(N_\Omega)^0$ is an open subgroup, geometrically irreducible, and commutes with field extension. Put $V=U_\Omega\cap C$, a nonempty open subgroup of $C$. For any geometric point $x$ of $C$, work over its algebraically closed field: the two nonempty opens $V$ and $xV$ of the irreducible base change of $C$ intersect. A geometric point $y$ of their intersection has $y=xz$ for some $z\in V$, so $x=yz^{-1}\in U_\Omega$. Thus $C\subseteq U_\Omega$. The connected image $f_\Omega(G_\Omega)$ contains the identity, hence lies in $C$ and therefore in $U_\Omega$. On the generic fibre $j_F$ is an isomorphism, so $f_F$ also lands in $U_F$. The generic and closed fibres exhaust $T$; hence $f(G)\subseteq U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to factor $f=j\widetilde v$ uniquely with $\widetilde v:G\to H$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), identity subgroup and geometric irreducibility; elementary intersecting-open-translates argument; Schemes Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens) and Tag 01IK (lemma-open-subspace-scheme), factorization through an open subscheme.

proof.text: An open immersion is a monomorphism by its identification with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Compose the multiplication identity for $\widetilde v$ with $j$: it becomes the identity for $f$ and $j$, so monicity proves it; the same argument gives the unit and inverse identities. Thus $\widetilde v$ is a group homomorphism. Generically, $\alpha j_F=1_P$ and $\alpha f_F=v$ give $\widetilde v_F=v$. If $w:G\to H$ is another extension, then $jw$ and $f$ have the same generic restriction. The injectivity in [lem-sfb-semiabelian-neron-lft-existence], applied to the smooth scheme $G$, gives $jw=f=j\widetilde v$; monicity gives $w=\widetilde v$.

source.place: Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models (1990), 10.1 Definition 1 (printed p.289) and 10.2 Theorem 2 (printed p.297), specialized to geometrically semiabelian groups. Local copy WANTED; primary-source scan read online at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf, PDF pages 296 and 304. The criterion uses absence of an additive subgroup after completed strict henselian fraction-field extension, which holds for a geometrically semiabelian group.

A closure computation over the snapshot (919 nodes) reaches neither the item nor the twin, so there is no cycle; live still has the item unsplit and the twin citing it. The statement is unchanged and no re-split note applies. The four steps were checked. Step 1: P=H_F is smooth (lem-pc-proper-base-change (2)), separated and of finite type (elementary), and semiabelian by the def, which quantifies over all algebraically closed fields; the new Néron node gives j and f with αj_F=1 and αf_F=v. Step 2: the open-immersion node applies with A=H, B=N, a=j; all hypotheses hold and N needs no finite type. Step 3: G_Ω is connected by power-integrality at n=1, whose hypotheses hold (an abelian variety is a proper smooth connected group, commutative as an fppf quotient). Identity-component node on N_Ω: open translates of V meet, giving C⊆U_Ω and then f(G)⊆U, and the map factors through the open subscheme (Mathlib leaf). Step 4: monicity of the open immersion gives the homomorphism identities and v~_F=v; uniqueness comes from Néron injectivity on the smooth G. New node lem-sfb-semiabelian-neron-lft-existence matches BLR 10.1 Def 1 and 10.2 Thm 2, which hold for any DVR. The no-G_a condition holds because a G_a maps trivially to a torus and to an abelian variety. Commutativity and the homomorphism clause follow from uniqueness; the G_m case shows lft is needed. New node lem-sfb-generically-isomorphic-semiabelian-open-immersion is true by an independent proof: ℓ-power torsion of ker a_s lifts over R^sh, and rigidity of étale sections in the separated B[ℓ^m] gives a quasi-finite kernel. ZMT for a birational map to a normal B then gives an open immersion. The semiabelian source excludes the counterexample G_a with multiplication by π. Neither new node duplicates or restates the item (rg over the snapshot and live: no Néron or similar criterion node). The normal-base generalization depends on the item, so citing it would make a cycle. Batch 5: power-integrality reaches lem-trf-smooth-composition, which is generic composition of smooth morphisms, outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions, so accepted. No SGA citation; tool_uses (proper-base-change (2), open-subscheme factorization leaf) accepted. BLR, Conrad and Faltings are not in the local literature (marked WANTED); BLR was checked from memory of the text.

lean.statement:
theorem semiabelian_trait_hom_extension
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra R L] [IsFractionRing R L]
    (G H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of R)))) [IsCommMonObj G.X] [IsCommMonObj H.X]
    [Smooth G.X.hom] [IsSeparated G.X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom]
    [Smooth H.X.hom] [IsSeparated H.X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation H.X.hom] [QuasiCompact H.X.hom]
    (hG : HasSemiabelianGeometricFibres G)
    (hH : HasSemiabelianGeometricFibres H)
    (v : (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R L)))).mapGrp.obj G ⟶
      (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R L)))).mapGrp.obj H) :
    ∃! vbar : G ⟶ H,
      (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R L)))).mapGrp.map vbar = v
lean.note: Exact existing declaration, already landed for lem-sfb-semiabelian-trait-hom-extension. Renaming the fraction field L to F changes no hypothesis or conclusion. LocallyOfFinitePresentation and QuasiCompact, together with IsSeparated, express finite presentation. Uses the canonical group-object base-change functor and unique extension as an actual group homomorphism. No module is added; see report for the shared declaration and the independent proof-plan handoff.
